project.title: Native password-bound MFA enrollment ceremony
project.goal: Complete native password-bound MFA enrollment without provisional session and disclose backup codes only after confirmed commit
project.scope: R04/R41 internal admitted-control initial/unverified enrollment; no public endpoints/management/actual handle admission

boundary.responsibility: Separate password-bound setup authority from enrolled session authority and atomically confirm MFA
boundary.rationale: Unenrolled users need a complete native ceremony before the backend can replace hosted authentication

scenario.normal.description: Password begin returns only pending cookie/URI; valid TOTP atomically enables MFA, revokes old sessions and returns new session/codes after commit

scenario.given: Canonical synthetic control, verified active unenrolled identity and injected trusted runtime
scenario.when: Execute native password-bound setup and OTP confirmation across independent control processes
scenario.then: Password begin returns only pending cookie/URI; valid TOTP atomically enables MFA, revokes old sessions and returns new session/codes after commit

action.mfa_enrollment.description: Begin and confirm a distinct native MFA enrollment ceremony

errors.refused: Opaque invalid_credentials, invalid_control, connection_refused, auth crypto/clock errors; known committed Rejected vs NotCommitted/OutcomeUnknown failures

preconditions: Caller owns actually admitted control/workspace lifetime; runtime supplies trusted cookie/keyring/clock/issuer, not request identity claims
No live dual writers or silent adoption of enabled/NULL/duplicate factors
postconditions: Begin has no session/MFA authority or code disclosure; successful confirmation returns secrets only after known atomic commit
Refusals preserve the declared failure budget and original data; commit uncertainty retires the handle and withholds secrets
external_effects: Declared canonical control verification/session/twoFactor/telemetry mutations and existing immutable lifecycle triggers

authorization.rationale: Current identity/revocation, one-time challenge/code consumption and committed rejection counters require one serialized control transaction
